jobs.title: DIRECTOR OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
jobs.description:
About The Lacroix Medical Group

A leader in private medicine in Quebec, the Lacroix Medical Group comprises three rapidly growing divisions:

Medical Clinics
Operating Rooms
Biomedical Laboratory

The organization has experienced strong and sustained growth since its founding in 2009 and currently employs nearly 350 people. As part of its strategic plan, the Group aims to accelerate its national and international development.

OUR MISSION

To be the benchmark in private healthcare.

OUR VALUES

Passion | Respect | Integrity | Commitment | Innovation.

The Mandate

In a context of sustained growth and transformation of its activities, Lacroix Medical Group is seeking a Director of Information Technology who will actively contribute to the organization's technological evolution.

Reporting directly to the President and CEO, the Director of IT plays a strategic role across the entire network. They are responsible for defining, structuring, and developing the IT function to effectively support the organization's operations, growth, and ambitions.

They provide leadership for technology strategy, infrastructure, business systems, cybersecurity, data governance, digital transformation, and artificial intelligence.

He is also responsible for the performance of his team and the organization's technology partner ecosystem. This role is for an experienced, business-oriented, and results-driven IT leader who can combine strategic vision with excellent execution. Your Key Responsibilities IT Strategy and Governance: Define and deploy the IT vision and master plan in line with the strategic, operational, and financial priorities of Groupe médical Lacroix. Advise senior management on investments, risks, and key technological choices.

Performance and Business Continuity

Ensure the performance, robustness, and high availability of the infrastructure and technology platforms essential to the network's medical and administrative activities, including ERP, CRM, DME, LIS, SaaS, and cloud environments.

Digital Transformation, Data, and Artificial Intelligence

Identify and prioritize initiatives to transform the organization through technology, data valorization, automation, and artificial intelligence. Lead major technology projects and ensure their effective integration into operations.

Cybersecurity and Risk Management

Maintain high standards in cybersecurity, information protection, redundancy, and business continuity in an environment where system availability and the protection of medical data are critical.

Leadership and Organizational Performance

Lead and develop a competent, autonomous, and accountable IT team. Establish clear objectives and performance indicators, ensure rigorous budget management, and optimize the contribution of suppliers, consultants, and technology partners.

An Executive Role Close to Operations

At Lacroix Medical Group, technology must meet the realities on the ground.

The IT Director will therefore need to maintain close contact with the various business units and network teams to understand their needs, anticipate challenges, and ensure that technological solutions contribute concretely to operational performance and service quality.

The position consequently requires excellent mobility. The successful candidate will be required to travel regularly throughout the Lacroix network in Quebec to meet with teams, support projects, and remain connected to the operational realities of the various facilities.

This on-the-ground presence is an essential component of the role and not an occasional responsibility.

The mandate expressly includes regular visits to service points.

The Ideal Candidate

We are looking for an experienced manager with a strong business acumen and excellent technological expertise, recognized for their leadership, judgment, and ability to drive organizational growth.

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

A bachelor's degree in computer engineering, computer science, or a related field;
15 to 20 years of experience in information technology, including a minimum of 5 years in a management role;
Mastery of software architecture and project management;
A solid understanding of multi-site and cloud infrastructures;
Good knowledge of SaaS environments and major business platforms: ERP, CRM, financial systems, telephony, Microsoft 365, and others;
A thorough understanding of the issues cybersecurity, data governance and valorization, and artificial intelligence;
Proven experience in team management and development;
Recognized leadership in transformation and change management;
Ability to prioritize, make decisions, and manage effectively in a complex and evolving environment;
Excellent business acumen and the ability to communicate technological issues to senior management;
Fluency in French and English, both written and spoken;
A valid driver's license, a vehicle, and significant availability for regular travel throughout the network.

The Leader Profile We Are Looking For

Beyond technological expertise, we are looking for someone who stands out for their ability to mobilize, structure, and deliver.

A positive and committed leader with a strong sense of Accountability, the ability to build high-performing teams, manage rigorously, challenge the status quo, and transform technological challenges into concrete solutions for the business. The IT Director must be equally comfortable discussing strategy with senior management and understanding the challenges faced by teams in the field. Conditions and Compensation Lacroix Medical Group offers a competitive total compensation package including: Annual salary of $140,000 to $175,000, depending on experience and expertise; 4 weeks of vacation and 4 paid personal days; RRSP+ program with employer contribution; Cell phone allowance; Lacroix Health Credit; and an annual Lacroix gift card. This benefit can be combined with other benefits for personalized medical services.

Business travel expense account for trips outside your usual work area

Join a growing network and become a key player in the future of private medicine in Quebec.

Apply now and make a real difference.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Enterprise Execution
jobs.description:
Join a Challenger

At EQ, we're remaking banking so every Canadian gets ahead, every day. Serving nearly 4 million Canadians from coast to coast, we offer a wide variety of financial services from banking and lending, to trust and credit union solutions.

We've been at this since 1970, challenging the conventions of traditional banking with smarter, faster, and more connected financial experiences.

What's kept us moving?
The people behind it all: challengers who ask better questions, push back on old assumptions, and look for a better way forward.

If you're driven to help reshape how banking works for Canadians and the businesses that power our economy, this could be your next big opportunity.

We can’t wait to get to know you!

The Work

The Senior Director, Enterprise Execution is responsible for helping EQB translate strategic priorities into business outcomes.

Working directly with executive leaders across the organization, this role leads a focused portfolio of the Bank's most important enterprise initiatives and strategic priorities. These are high-impact, cross-functional efforts that are critical to delivering EQB's strategy, growth ambitions, and financial objectives. The role serves as a bridge between strategy, execution, and outcomes, ensuring that the Bank's biggest priorities maintain momentum, overcome obstacles, and deliver the impact they were intended to achieve.

Enterprise Execution acts as an execution partner to leadership, bringing structured problem-solving, strategic thinking, and execution discipline to a select group of enterprise priorities. The role combines elements of strategy execution, enterprise leadership, organizational effectiveness, and executive problem-solving, helping translate strategic ambition into measurable results.

The ideal candidate combines the structured problem-solving capabilities of a top-tier strategy consultant with the practical execution mindset of an experienced operator. They are highly comfortable working in ambiguous situations, quickly building credibility with senior stakeholders, and driving progress on complex challenges that cut across multiple business units. They are intellectually curious, commercially minded, and action-oriented. They know how to move seamlessly between strategy and execution, challenge and support, analysis and action. Most importantly, they have a demonstrated ability to help organizations deliver on their most important priorities and achieve meaningful outcomes.

Strategic Initiative Leadership & Enterprise Priorities (55%)

Lead a portfolio of EQB's highest-priority enterprise initiatives and strategic priorities, including CEO- and CFO-sponsored programs.
Partner directly with executive sponsors and act as a trusted advisor to mobilize, accelerate, and deliver initiatives that are critical to achieving the Bank's strategic and financial objectives.
Provide hands-on leadership for complex cross-functional initiatives requiring enterprise coordination, senior stakeholder alignment, and disciplined execution.
Shape implementation approaches, execution strategies, operating models, and delivery plans to maximize organizational impact.
Challenge assumptions, strengthen plans, and improve decision-making through structured problem solving and rigorous analysis.
Identify and resolve issues, risks, dependencies, and organizational barriers that could impede successful execution.
Bring an enterprise-wide perspective that helps ensure initiatives advance broader corporate objectives.

Strategic Execution & Outcome Realization (25%)

Ensure approved business cases and strategic objectives translate into measurable business, customer, operational, and financial outcomes.
Partner with initiative leaders to strengthen execution plans and improve the likelihood of successful outcomes.
Identify emerging risks, dependencies, and barriers requiring intervention and help drive resolution.
Provide executive visibility into initiative progress, key decisions, and areas requiring leadership attention.
Work closely with Finance, initiative owners, and business leaders to understand expected versus realized outcomes and identify opportunities to improve performance.
Conduct initiative reviews and post-implementation assessments to reinforce accountability and continuous improvement.
Promote a culture of disciplined execution and ownership across enterprise priorities.

Enterprise Planning & Prioritization (10%)

Lead the annual enterprise initiative prioritization process as part of EQB's strategic planning cycle.
Partner with business leaders, Finance, and Strategy teams to identify, evaluate, and prioritize initiatives requiring investment and organizational capacity.
Facilitate discussions regarding sequencing, trade-offs, resource allocation, and execution readiness.
Develop an integrated view of enterprise priorities, dependencies, and investment requirements to support executive decision-making.
Help ensure organizational focus remains concentrated on initiatives that create the greatest strategic impact.

Executive & Board Effectiveness (10%)

Help ensure EQB's most important strategic priorities, enterprise initiatives, and investment decisions are supported by clear, aligned, and decision-ready executive and Board materials.
Partner with senior leaders across the organization to elevate the quality, consistency, and strategic coherence of materials presented to Executive Leadership Team and Board forums.
Ensure major strategic discussions are informed by a cohesive enterprise perspective and supported by fact-based, well-structured recommendations.
Challenge gaps, inconsistencies, duplication, and disconnects across strategic updates, investment proposals, and enterprise initiatives before they reach decision-making forums.
Support major strategic planning sessions, Board strategy discussions, and executive reviews by helping ensure discussions remain focused on decisions, outcomes, and enterprise priorities.
Act as a steward of excellence for the Bank's most important leadership discussions and governance forums.

Let's Talk About You!

8-10 years of experience in strategy consulting, corporate strategy, enterprise execution, strategic initiatives, business transformation, operating leadership, or related fields.
Demonstrated track record leading complex cross-functional initiatives that deliver measurable business outcomes.
Experience partnering with executive leadership teams and influencing decisions in highly matrixed organizations.
Strong commercial, financial, and operational acumen.
Proven ability to drive alignment, solve complex problems, and deliver results without direct authority.
Exceptional communication and executive presentation skills.
Experience developing executive and Board-level recommendations and materials.

Preferred Experience

Experience in private equity value creation roles or at a top-tier management consulting firm a significant asset.
Experience within financial services, banking, fintech, or other complex regulated industries.
Experience leading enterprise-wide strategic initiatives, operating model changes, integration programs, or growth-focused initiatives.
Familiarity with strategic planning, capital allocation, benefits realization, and organizational prioritization processes.
MBA or equivalent graduate degree considered an asset.

What we offer [For full-time permanent roles]

💰 Competitive discretionary bonus

✨ Market leading RRSP match program

🩺 Medical, dental, vision, life, and disability benefits

📝 Employee Share Purchase Plan

👶🏽 Maternity/Parental top-up while you care for your little one

🏝 Generous vacation policy and personal days

🖥 Virtual events to connect with your fellow colleagues

🎓 Professional development and comprehensive Career Development program

💛 A fulfilling opportunity to join one of the top FinTechs and help create a new kind of banking experience

The incumbent will be working hybrid and in office time will be spent working from EQ Bank’s additional office space located at 2200-25 Ontario Street, Toronto, ON
.

Equity, Diversity & Inclusion

EQ is committed to building an inclusive, accessible environment where every employee feels valued, respected, and supported. We believe our organization is stronger — and our people thrive — when we honour and celebrate diverse experiences, identities, and perspectives. We’re equally committed to supporting your growth, both professionally and personally.

We provide a barrier‑free recruitment process and work environment. If you require accommodations at any stage, we will work with you to ensure you can bring your best self to the process and beyond.

As part of our recruitment process, EQ uses AI to help screen, assess, and/or select applicants for this position. All AI-enabled outputs are reviewed and validated by our talent team. All candidates considered for hire must successfully complete a criminal background check and credit check. While we appreciate every application, an EQ recruiter will contact only those whose skills and experience most closely match the requirements of the role.

EQB Inc. (TSX: EQB) is the parent company of Equitable Bank, the country's seventh-largest Schedule I bank by assets, which operates EQ Bank, Canada's Challenger Bank™. EQB Inc. serves nearly 4 million Canadians and manages approximately $150 billion in combined assets under management and administration.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Capital Investment Strategy
jobs.description:
Toronto Pearson is transforming. Now’s the time for your career to fly.

The Greater Toronto Airports Authority (GTAA) is a unique and dynamic place to work, with a bold plan to make Toronto Pearson, Canada’s leading global hub airport, a global leader in airport performance, customer care and sustainability. Together with our partners, approximately 2,100 GTAA employees are working to create a next-generation airport by innovating in all we do and striving for the most uplifting, safe and efficient experience for our passengers – all while championing the prosperity of our people, the community we call home, and our aviation partners. Join us on our journey together, as we put the joy back into travel and make Toronto Pearson the chosen place to fly and work.

What's in it for you?

An opportunity to grow, develop, and thrive within a dynamic, and fast-growing company alongside thoughtful and passionate individuals dedicated to their work and community.
Comprehensive benefits, including a flexible retirement program with employer matching, along with voluntary savings options (RRSP, TFSA, and Non-Registered Savings Plans).
A flexible hybrid work environment, continuous internal and external learning opportunities, and a meaningful reward and recognition program.

What can you expect from this position?

Reporting to the Executive Director, Capital Planning, the Associate Director, Capital Investment Strategy will lead the Capital Investments function and help determine where and why Toronto Pearson invests. You will provide financial leadership across the front end of the capital investment lifecycle by supporting strategic initiative business cases, portfolio prioritization, project intake, investment governance, and benefits realization. Working with business units, the Transformation Office, Strategy, Finance business partners, and program teams, you will translate strategic priorities into decision-ready investment recommendations for executive consideration. You will establish consistent methodologies, standards, and controls so that capital investments are strategically aligned, financially sound, affordable, and supported by reliable data and robust business intelligence.

As an Associate Director, Capital Investment Strategy, you will:

Lead the development and financial evaluation of business cases for major strategic initiatives, while establishing the standards and methodologies applied across the broader capital portfolio.
Develop complex financial models incorporating NPV, IRR, ROIC, cash flow, sensitivity, scenario, and risk-adjusted investment analyses.
Challenge assumptions and translate complex analysis into decision-ready recommendations for executive and Board-level consideration.
Lead quarterly financial forecasting and reporting for multi-year strategic initiatives.
Support the enterprise capital allocation and prioritization process with a multidisciplinary team, applying consistent strategic, financial, affordability, risk, and delivery-capacity criteria to recommend investments, sequencing decisions, trade-offs, and off-ramp actions to executive governance forums.
Establish and maintain enterprise investment-governance standards, including business-case methodologies and templates, evaluation criteria, capital allocation frameworks, hurdle rates, risk premiums, stage-gate requirements, and decision records that support consistent and transparent recommendations.
Lead the enterprise project intake and triage process partnering with the appropriate teams to confirm strategic alignment, scope maturity, resource capacity, accounting treatment, funding pathway, and business-case requirements before investments advance for prioritization or approval.
Establish benefits and cost baselines for approved investments, integrate expected outcomes into portfolio planning, monitor realization across all programs, and lead post-investment evaluations that identify variances, lessons learned, and implications for future capital allocation decisions.
Support the evaluation of public-private partnerships and alternative delivery models, including financial returns, affordability, financing approaches, and risk allocation.
Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team while fostering accountability, collaboration, analytical excellence, and continuous improvement.

This is the role for you, if you have:

A university degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
A CPA, CFA, CBV, MBA, or other relevant professional designation or graduate degree is considered an asset.
Five or more years of relevant experience in investment analysis, corporate finance, infrastructure finance, business-case development, portfolio planning, or major capital programs, including experience leading complex, cross-functional investment decisions in a leadership capacity.
Advanced expertise in financial modelling, scenario analysis, sensitivity testing, and investment evaluation methodologies.
Expertise in developing decision-ready business cases for major strategic or capital initiatives.
Demonstrated experience designing or operating capital allocation, project intake, stage-gate, investment-governance, or benefits-realization processes across a complex portfolio.
Experience evaluating public-private partnerships or alternative capital-project delivery and financing models.
Advanced stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the ability to work effectively across senior leadership and business functions.
Strong executive communication skills and the ability to translate complex financial analysis into clear business implications and recommendations.
Strategic thinking, sound judgement, and strong problem-solving and decision-making capabilities.
Experience leading, coaching, and developing finance professionals in a collaborative environment.
The ability to obtain and retain Transportation Security Clearance at the designated level for the position.

The GTAA is committed to Employment Equity and maintaining a diverse, equitable and inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive.

This position is exempt from Ontario's 2026 pay transparency requirements under Regulation 476/24.

jobs.description:
Turner & Townsend is a global professional services company with over 22,000 people in more than 60 countries.

Working with our clients across real estate, infrastructure, energy and natural resources, we transform together delivering outcomes that improve people’s lives. Working in partnership makes it possible to deliver the world’s most impactful projects and programmes as we turn challenge into opportunity and complexity into success.

Our capabilities include programme, project, cost, asset and commercial management, controls and performance, procurement and supply chain, net zero and digital solutions.

We are majority-owned by CBRE Group, Inc., the world’s largest commercial real estate services and investment firm, with our partners holding a significant minority interest. Turner & Townsend and CBRE work together to provide clients with the premier programme, project and cost management offering in markets around the world.

As a Turner & Townsend Project Management Director, you’ll be responsible for client management and department-related management services within multiple geographic markets, programs, and asset classes to achieve the company's strategic business objectives by delivering outstanding results to our client.

This job is part of the Enterprise Project Management division. They are responsible for the management of projects from initiation through completion for dedicated client groups as part of a multi-service outsourcing contract. You will be responsible for global teams delivering commercial office fit-out, retail and Move Adds & Change services.

Who are you?

You are an expert Real Estate
Project Management Director
with a minimum of 12+
years post-graduate experience
in real estate project management
looking for the next step or are currently undertaking a similar role in a similar environment.

Job Description

Communicate with the client and manage client expectations on resourcing needs, project and programme performance, risks, status reporting, and issues escalation
Direct all phases of the delivery process for large and high-profile clients including procurement, contracting, planning, tracking, and execution
Provide formal supervision to direct report employees in Canada, the US and EMEA. Monitor the training and development of staff. Conduct performance evaluations and coaching. Oversee the recruiting and hiring of new employees.
Coordinate and manage the team's daily activities. Establish work schedules, assign tasks, and cross-train staff. Set and track staff and department deadlines. Mentor and coach as needed.
Ensure that contract procurement, negotiation, execution, administration, and closeouts are accurate, timely, and compliant.
Develop new business growth and maintain existing business relationships.
Maintain full responsibility for the financial performance of market, program, and client accounts.

Apply deep knowledge of multiple disciplines, broad industry knowledge, and commercial awareness. Drive financial and functional performance within disciplines and across business.
Lead by example and model behaviors that are consistent with Turner & Townsend values. Conceptualize new methods, techniques, processes, and standards across job disciplines or functions.
Direct the resolution of highly complex or unusual business problems by applying advanced critical thinking.
Work in partnership with the Account Alliance Director, Facility Management teams, Transaction teams, Procurement and other teams to provide a fully integrated and seamless service.
Ensure that all account KPI’s and SLA’s are achieved.

Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree preferred with 12-15 years of relevant real estate project delivery experience. In lieu of a degree, a combination of experience and education will be considered. LEED AP, PMP, and/or CCM designation(s) preferred.
Polished communicator with experience presenting and liaising with client executive and C-Suite level employees.
In-depth knowledge of financial terms and principles and the ability to analyze the most complex business/financial data and develop innovative solutions.
Experience in the areas of staffing, selection, training, development, coaching, mentoring, measuring, appraising, and rewarding performance and retention is preferred.
Ability to exchange sensitive, complicated, and difficult information, convey performance expectations and handle problems.
Leadership skills to motivate the team to achieve broad operational targets with impacts on own job discipline, multiple job disciplines, and department.
In-depth knowledge of Microsoft Office products. Examples include Word, Excel, Outlook, etc.
Expert organizational skills with an unrivaled inquisitive mindset.

jobs.title: vCIO - Virtual Chief Information Officer
jobs.description:
About F12:
F12 was built by uniting IT consulting firms across Canada with a shared vision: to reduce risk and complexity by crafting technology platforms that empower leaders to focus and thrive. We elevate IT conversations from ingredients to outcomes, delivering fully designed solutions with no bad options. If you’re looking for the fast lane into an IT career or want to supercharge your professional development, you’ve come to the right place. At F12, you’ll collaborate with a diverse team and gain exposure to technology services across countless businesses—building a resume rich with experience and accomplishments. Our mission is to elevate our employees by building and retaining an elite team of IT professionals equipped to deliver unmatched service to Canadian business leaders. We value humble service, continuous improvement, and hard work—and we’re looking for like-minded individuals to join us.

The Purpose:
As the vCIO, you will support F12’s top tier clients in providing consultation for technical strategy and ensure that we are engaging our clients in a way that aligns them with F12’s offerings, while continually driving their IT strategies forward. This role assists clients in maximizing IT investment through exploring, introducing and evaluating available technology solutions and automation in order to enhance and streamline operations.

The vCIO is naturally inquisitive and will analyze how various technology enhancements can benefit a client, providing suggestions for optimal solutions. They oversee the client’s entire IT infrastructure, ensuring their network is running smoothly. They will ensure documentation is up to date and assist with service analysts, upgrades, and conversions to F12 program compliance, as required. The vCIO will partner and build strong relationships with all key stakeholders, such as with their assigned client base, Technical Account Manager and Integrated Service Team (IST) Managers to ensure alignment and to provide invaluable strategies to improve the health of the client’s business and their technology needs.

Responsibilities

Cybersecurity: Implement comprehensive cybersecurity strategies to protect the clients from various cyber threats and identify gaps for improved security measures
Technology Budget Planning: Oversee the management of IT budgets for the client-base, ensuring cost-effective use of IT resources
Hardware/Software Upgrades and Replacements: Manage client upgrade and replacement of hardware and software to ensure optimal performance and security
Vendor Selection: Oversee the selection and management of client IT vendors, preferability utilizing F12 partnerships, to ensure high-quality services
Company Growth and Expansion: Support the organization's growth and expansion into new markets through strategic IT planning and implementation
Backup, Disaster Recovery, and Business Continuity: Implement solutions for backup, disaster recovery, and business continuity which meet F12 standards and the business needs of our clients
Overall IT Strategy: Develop an overall IT strategy that aligns with and supports the client business objectives by creation of a comprehensive technology road map
Revenue Growth: Work towards increasing the your book of business by X% revenue per year through by identifying solution gaps in supported clients
Outside Sales Support: Working closely with our skilled F12 sales associates, you will assist with uncovering business needs to ensure appropriate solutions are designed for incoming clients
Internal Mentorship: Provide mentorship to internal team members to foster skill development and knowledge sharing
Internal Initiatives: Drive internal initiatives to improve processes, services, and client satisfaction

Requirements

Background in designing/developing IT systems and planning IT implementation
Strong understanding of varied requirements of F12’s Client base
Strong strategic and business mindset
Stay current on technology innovations and trends
Awareness of financial management and business cases (budget, P&L, understanding ROI)
Professional presentation and communication skills
Solid understanding of data analysis and business operations
Proactive thinker with superior analytical and problem-solving capabilities
Ability to understand business needs and conduct meaningful conversations.
Agility to work in a team environment, and the autonomy to work independently with minimal supervision.
Consistent time management skills and the capacity to manage due date commitments.
5+ years of experience or understanding of IT Managed Services industry.
Industry certifications and a willingness to pursue continual education.

What You Can Expect from Us:
We are proud of our forward-thinking, dynamic culture that champions diversity, inclusivity, and a respectful working environment. We also want to make sure that however you get IT done in all parts of your life, we’ve got your back. Our comprehensive total rewards program includes:

Work-Life & Growth: Three weeks vacation plus extra Flex Days, leadership development opportunities, growth coaching, and reimbursements for educational advancement and certifications.
Health & Financial Well-Being: Health Spending Account or RRSP matching, extended health care, dental and vision coverage, disability and life insurance, and an employee assistance program.
Additional Perks: Tuition reimbursement, paid time off, on-site parking, high-class office amenities, and company events.

jobs.title: Director of Strategic Finance
jobs.description:
About Forma.ai:
  Forma.ai is a Series B startup that's revolutionizing how sales compensation is designed, managed and optimized. We handle billions in annual managed commissions for market leaders like Edmentum, Stryker, and Autodesk. 
Our growth has been fuelled by our passion for fundamentally changing and shaping how companies use sales intelligence to drive business strategy.  
We’re welcoming equally driven individuals who are excited about creating something big!  
DIRECTOR OF STRATEGIC FINANCE

Strategic FP&A, AI Automation, & Executive-Level Storytelling
ABOUT THE ROLE:

We are looking for an exceptional, hands-on Director of Strategic Finance to act as the strategic right-hand lead to our VP of Finance. Operating alongside our Controller (who leads accounting close, statutory compliance, tax, and ERP administration), you will own our forward-looking financial strategy. You will lead our corporate modelling, deploy AI and modern automation workflows across Finance and RevOps, execute on M&A and capital markets transactions, and use generative AI or AI applications to build out high-performance analytics frameworks as the company scales.
WHAT YOU'LL DO (KEY RESPONSIBILITIES):

1. Hands-On Strategic FP&A & Corporate Modeling
• Corporate Financial Architecture: Build and maintain our dynamic 3-statement models, weekly/monthly/quarterly operating plans, revenue forecasting, multi-year operating forecasts, and scenario analyses from the ground up without relying on junior analysts.
• Executive & Board Presentation: Spearhead the quantitative financial narrative, analysis, and materials for Board of Directors meetings, executive quarterly reviews, and investor reporting.
• Corporate Planning: Lead the annual budgeting process by working with the executive team to develop an annual plan with near real-time reporting on plan progress.
• Future Team Foundation: Establish rigorous modeling standards and analytical infrastructure today, with the mandate to hire, mentor, and build out an FP&A and FinOps team over the next 1–2 years.
2. Financial Engineering & AI Workflow Automation
• AI Agent & Workflow Deployment: Identify manual bottlenecks across billing, contract parsing, data extraction, and commercial operations; build and deploy LLM workflows, custom prompts, and automated scripts.
• Data Pipeline & Systems Integration: Architect and optimize data flows connecting CRM (Salesforce/HubSpot), CPQ, Billing, and ERP systems to automate revenue operations and eliminate reconciliation friction.
• Modern Automation Tooling: Use tools like Python, SQL, Zapier/Make, and API integrations to establish self-sustaining, real-time reporting layers.
• AI Analytics & Insights: Leverage AI to drive deeper analysis and insights throughout the organization (i.e. QBR’s, MMR’s, BvA’s)
3. RevOps & Commercial Structuring
• GTM Engine Analytics: Partner with RevOps to track and analyze sales capacity, pipeline velocity, CAC/LTV dynamics, and retention cohorts.
• Deal Structuring & Deal Desk: Serve as the primary strategic finance partner to Sales and RevOps on deal structuring, pricing models, margin analysis, discounting schedules, and commercial contract terms.
4. M&A / Capital Markets Execution & Compensation Modelling

• Transaction & Valuation Execution: Own the operational execution for M&A / capital market transactions, including due diligence financial modelling, virtual data room (VDR) setup, and cap table administration
• Compensation Architecture: Model and maintain corporate compensation bands, incentive structures, and equity option pool dilution economics.

WHO YOU ARE (QUALIFICATIONS):

- 7–10+ years in Strategic Finance, FP&A, BizOps, or Investment Banking / Management Consulting followed by high-growth B2B SaaS operational experience. Strong business acumen with a high intellectual curiosity.
- FP&A Mastery:
Spreadsheet wizard with demonstrated mastery of complex revenue modelling, 3-statement modelling, operational modelling, SaaS metrics (ARR, NRR, GRR, CAC payback), and executive-level financial storytelling.
- Engineering & AI Mindset:
Practical experience architecting the finance tech stack and working with data, deploying AI/LLM tools, automation platforms (Python, SQL, Zapier/Make), and SaaS toolchains (Salesforce, Stripe/Chargebee, NetSuite) to eliminate manual workflows.
- Commercial Depth:
Proven deal desk and commercial contract experience, with a solid grasp of pricing models, billing schedules, and equity compensation economics.
- Autonomy & Drive:
High-autonomy builder who thrives with ambiguity and enjoys executing hands-on work from scratch with the leadership aptitude to manage direct reports as the team grows.

WHY THIS ROLE IS DIFFERENT:

You won't be managing month-end reconciliations, audits, tax filings, or HR administration—our Controller leads those domains with excellence. You are joining to be an operational architect and strategic partner: designing intelligent financial infrastructure, building board-level models, and leveraging AI to scale our operational engine.

Growth.
You’ll have a huge opportunity to build a career for yourself and gain the type of experience you’re looking for, whether that’s as an individual contributor or as a people leader.

We believe complacency breeds failure, so we set new goals as quickly as we achieve them. We persist in the face of adversity, learn from our mistakes, and push each other to continuously improve. The status-quo is kryptonite.
Love our tech. Love our customers.
Our platform solves a very complex problem in a currently underserved market. While everyone at Forma isn’t customer-facing, we’re all customer-focused. Maybe even slightly customer-obsessed. ­

Currently, Forma.ai does not use artificial intelligence as part of our recruitment process, specifically but not limited to the screening, filtering and shortlisting of applicants.

  Forma is a proud equal opportunity employer that is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment.   Every effort to accommodate candidates for accessibility will be made upon request.
